findings.title: Untrusted feed/remote HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import passes feed or remotely fetched HTML directly to PostCreator with cook_method raw_html, and Post#cook returns that raw value as cooked. PollFeed supplies RSS/Atom content with no HTML sanitization, and the normal post rendering path trusts cooked HTML. A malicious or compromised feed item containing a script event handler or other active markup can therefore be stored and executed in the browsers of users viewing the resulting topic, not only in the embed view.

findings.title: Referer is interpolated unsafely and incorrectly as postMessage targetOrigin
findings.body: The layout inserts the full user-controlled request.referer into a JavaScript string as the targetOrigin for parent.postMessage. A referer containing a quote or script-breaking sequence can break out of the string and execute attacker JavaScript in the embed page. Even for legitimate referers, a full URL such as http://host/post-path is not a valid targetOrigin (which must be an origin), so browsers may reject the message and the parent iframe will never receive the resize height.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses reversed substring matching
findings.body: The handler accepts a message when discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) is not -1, i.e. when the sender origin is merely a substring of the configured Discourse URL string. Origin validation must be an exact origin comparison; substring matching accepts origins that are prefixes/substrings of the forum URL and is fragile with trailing slashes, ports, and look-alike hosts. A frame able to send a message from an accepted non-forum origin could resize the embed iframe unexpectedly.

findings.title: Embed view does not check whether the viewer can see the topic
findings.body: When a TopicEmbed exists, the controller builds a TopicView for that topic id and the embed template outputs raw post.cooked for its best posts. There is no guardian/can-see check comparable to the normal topic controller. If an originally public imported topic is later moved into a restricted category, made invisible, or otherwise access-controlled, anonymous visitors framing the embed from the allowed host can still read its best posts through /embed/best.

findings.title: PollFeed crashes on feed items without a content element
findings.body: The job unconditionally calls i.content.scrub and passes the result to CGI.unescapeHTML. Many RSS/Atom items expose only title/link/description or use a namespaced content field, so SimpleRSS can return nil for content. A single such item raises NoMethodError/TypeError and aborts the whole hourly poll, preventing all remaining items in that feed from being imported.

findings.title: TopicEmbed.import has a check-then-create race on embed_url
findings.body: Import first queries TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first and only later creates the row inside a block, while the migration adds a unique index on embed_url. Two concurrent retrievals or feed polls for the same new URL can both see no embed, both create topics/posts, and then one fails with RecordNotUnique on TopicEmbed.create!, rolling back or orphaning work after external effects/jobs have been enqueued. Concurrent imports for the same URL should be serialized or the uniqueness violation handled as an update.

findings.title: Controller spec expects synchronous TopicRetriever but controller enqueues a job
findings.body: The success example stubs TopicRetriever.new and expects retrieve to be called, but EmbedController#best now calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) and never references TopicRetriever directly. This example therefore fails against the implementation it ships with, and it leaves the actual enqueue arguments and loading-template behaviour unverified. The adjacent TopicView example also stubs TopicView.new to return nil, after which best.html.erb dereferences @topic_view.posts, so the success-path rendering is not genuinely exercised.

findings.title: Disqus import silently drops the category option and now requires fetching each source URL
findings.body: The thor command removes the documented -c/--category option, so existing import invocations passing it will now fail as an unknown switch. It also replaces local creation of the opening post from the Disqus export with TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...), which performs an HTTP fetch and readability extraction for every thread; threads whose link is blank, offline, blocked, or no longer readable produce no opening post and their Disqus replies are skipped entirely, whereas previously they were imported from the export file alone.
